literal: Twelfth month, day yiwei: an edict said: "The vulgar say Han Gaozu rose from common cloth and possessed all under Heaven — this does not reach the root of the matter.
idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the twelfth month an edict declared: "Common talk holds that Han Gaozu rose from the ranks and won the empire. That misses the point entirely.

literal: Liu inherited Yao's succession, virtue spanning ages without break; there were signs of serpent and dragon, responses of clouds and colors; the five planets gathered above, Heaven and man both in accord — a lord of bright revolution, the great fortune belled, cannot be sought by improper hope.
idiomatic: The house of Liu inherited the mandate of Yao. Heaven showed signs in serpent and dragon, clouds and the five planets aligned, and the age itself called for a new ruler. Such a throne is not won by naked ambition.

literal: Yet the mad and cunning, the reason they stumble and fall without end, are truly deluded by the tale of chasing the deer and blind to Heaven's mandate.
idiomatic: Yet rebels still fall because they believe the old tale that the empire is a deer for anyone to chase, and forget that the mandate belongs to Heaven alone.

literal: Therefore there are those who follow the track of overturned carts, tread the traces of treason and rebellion; where poison is severe they overturn provinces and commanderies, where harm is slight they ruin towns and villages; reaching even to body dead and name fallen, calamity reaching the nine clans — following disorder with the current, dying without regret. Is it not painful!
idiomatic: They follow the road of ruined kings, spread rebellion through town and province, destroy themselves and their kin to the ninth degree, and die unrepentant in the flood of disorder. What folly, and what pain!

literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals esteems the beauty of great unity; Wu and Chu presumptuously styled themselves and long received execution and extinction; the gentleman despised their false names, comparing them to dust and filth.
idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals praise unity and condemn usurpation. Wu and Chu took false titles and were destroyed; wise men held their names in contempt, no better than filth.

literal: Unless one succeeds a sage and bears virtue, Heaven and man unite in meeting — the enterprise of emperor and king, how could it be an empty response?
idiomatic: Unless a man unites heaven and man, succeeds the sages, and bears true virtue, how can imperial rule be anything but an empty pretense?

literal: Reviewing past and present, those unrighteous who sought improper hope only lost the way to preserve their houses and lay under the punishment of blade and saw.
idiomatic: History shows that every traitor who reached for the throne lost his house and died by the blade.

literal: Those with state and family, if they can indeed push away the term of rise and fall, examine that Heaven's mandate is not easy, observe how signs and responses are secretly bestowed, stop the evil words of competing pursuit, cut off the presumptuous license of treacherous heroes, think much of blessing in knowing when to stop — then they are near to divine wisdom.
idiomatic: Let every lord weigh the cycle of rise and fall, know that the mandate is not easily held, read the signs Heaven sends, reject the lure of rebellion, and find sufficiency in his station — then he nears wisdom.

literal: Thus one can preserve glory and salary through Heaven's years, flow remaining blessing to later generations.
idiomatic: So may he keep honor through his years and leave blessing to his descendants.

literal: Being so, then calamity and perversity have no cause to arise, why should arms and armor rise?
idiomatic: Then rebellion finds no foothold, and arms need never be raised.

literal: All coming generations, exert yourselves in warning this — can one not be cautious!"
idiomatic: Let all future ages take warning. Can any man be careless?"

literal: At that time the Grand Astrologer repeatedly memorialized that celestial patterns were disordered; the emperor personally viewed the classics of divination; many said change king, change government; therefore he repeatedly changed office titles — first to block and stop the fierce and cunning, second to dispel calamity and respond to change.
idiomatic: The grand astrologer reported disorder in the heavens; the emperor studied the prognostic texts himself, which spoke of change of dynasty. He therefore altered offices again and again, both to thwart traitors and to answer heaven's warnings.

literal: Before long, fearing the host below would be doubtful, hearts slandering and bellies dissenting, on day bingshen again an edict said: "The governance of high antiquity esteemed virtue and lowered names; there was appointment but no rank; easy to govern and affairs in order; therefore evil plots ceased and did not arise, treachery and villainy were cut off and did not act.
idiomatic: Fearing murmurs among his officers, on the bingshen day he issued another edict: "In high antiquity rulers valued virtue over titles. Offices were duties, not prizes. Evil plots died for want of reward, and treachery found no opening.

literal: At the end of Zhou of Ji, the lower overawed the upper and replaced them; by title they fixed themselves, by rank they regulated salary; ministers inherited their offices, grandees followed their affairs; yang virtue did not flourish, discussion arose from enriching families — therefore trouble arose from this, arms arose from this.
idiomatic: At the fall of Zhou the lower orders overturned their betters, made rank hereditary, and bought office with wealth. Yang virtue failed, families contended for power, and from that came rebellion and war.

literal: The defects of Qin and Han abandoned virtue and exalted extravagance; ability and inability mixed together, worthy and foolish confused; the hundred offices lost order, appointment not according to the man.
idiomatic: Qin and Han abandoned virtue for display, mixed the able with the worthless, and put the wrong men in office.

literal: Thereupon the way of loyalty and righteousness slept, the integrity of shame and honor was abandoned, the wind of yielding withdrew, discussions of ruin and praise arose — all without exception from esteeming and honoring name and rank, while calamity and defeat reached them.
idiomatic: Loyalty withered, shame died, modesty vanished, and slander flourished — all because men prized empty titles, and ruin followed.

literal: Anciently the Three Excellencies were set; duties great, worries heavy; therefore it is said 'awaiting punishment as chief minister' — intending to entrust responsibility and demand accomplishment, not empty favor and salary.
idiomatic: The Three Excellencies of old bore heavy trust and were called ministers 'awaiting punishment,' not men given empty honor.

literal: Yet in the present vulgar world, all take terrace and aide as glory and nobility, crane neck and seek them.
idiomatic: Today men crane their necks after the highest offices as if they were glory itself.

literal: These duties and offices rest in the lord of men alone to appoint; using them then they are heavy, discarding them then they are light.
idiomatic: These posts exist only at the sovereign's pleasure; in use they weigh, in disuse they are light.

literal: Thus offices have no constant name, while duties have fixed allotment — then what is honored reaches the utmost; why take the empty title of chief minister?
idiomatic: Office has no fixed glory; duty has a fixed measure. Honor lies in the work, not in the name of chief minister.

literal: Jie and Zhou facing south — though high yet could be held cheap.
idiomatic: Jie and Zhou sat facing south, yet their height deserved contempt.

literal: Duke of Zhou in low station — though humble yet could be honored.
idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou stood low, yet his humility deserved honor.

literal: One office can display wisdom; a wicker gate can leave a model.
idiomatic: Wisdom may shine in the lowest post; a wicker gate may leave a model to the age.

literal: If with morality and virtue as substance, one is worthier than overturned stew and a mat roof.
idiomatic: He who has virtue as his substance is greater than a king in a ruined house.

literal: Therefore he who measures himself ends with integrity and righteousness complete.
idiomatic: He who knows his measure dies whole in name and deed.

literal: He who is blind to profit — body trapped and name extinguished.
idiomatic: He who grasps at profit loses body and name together.

literal: Profit and name are the competing blemishes of ruin and praise.
idiomatic: Profit and fame breed slander and praise.

literal: The Way and virtue are the family treasure of spirit and knowledge.
idiomatic: The Way and virtue are the treasure of the wise.

literal: Therefore the Way and righteousness are the root of governance.
idiomatic: The Way and righteousness are the root of rule.

literal: Name and rank are the tip of governance.
idiomatic: Titles and ranks are only its branches.

literal: Name not rooted in the Way cannot be taken as fitting.
idiomatic: A title without the Way is unfit.

literal: Rank not supplementing the age cannot be taken as useful.
idiomatic: A rank that serves no need is useless.

literal: Using without prohibition — the illness is deep.
idiomatic: To use such men without restraint is a grave sickness.

literal: He who can penetrate its changes without losing what is correct — is it not the sage?
idiomatic: Only the sage can change with the times and yet keep to what is right.

literal: Coming generations, truly think on the principle of success and failure, examine the source of order and disorder, mirror the failures of Yin and Zhou, reform the defects of Qin and Han — then one is near to good governance."
idiomatic: Let later ages study success and failure, trace order and chaos to its source, learn from Yin, Zhou, Qin, and Han, and they will be near to good government."

literal: That year, Qifu Gangui was broken by Yao Xing; Li Gao privately styled Regional Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Liang.
idiomatic: That year Qifu Gangui was defeated by Yao Xing; Li Gao declared himself inspector of Liangzhou and duke of Liang.

literal: Year 4, spring, first month: Gaoche separate commander led his division of more than three thousand encampments to submit within the borders.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, in the first month of spring, a Gaoche sub-chief submitted with more than three thousand camps.

literal: Second month, day dinghai: ordered music masters to enter study dance, release vegetables at the Former Sage and Former Teacher.
idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the second month he ordered the music masters trained and performed the vegetable offering before the sage and teacher.

literal: On day dingyou, separately ordered envoys to tour provinces, hear and observe lawsuits, impeach the unlawful.
idiomatic: On the dingyou day he sent envoys through the provinces to hear lawsuits and impeach wrongdoers.

literal: Third month: the emperor personally fished, offered at the sleeping temple.
idiomatic: In the third month the emperor fished and offered at the sleeping temple.

literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinmao: abolished the Ye traveling secretariat.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the fourth month of summer he abolished the traveling secretariat at Ye.

literal: Ordered the relevant offices to clarify and raise the hidden and reclusive.
idiomatic: He ordered the ministries to seek out hidden worthies.

literal: Fifth month: began the Purple Pole Hall, Black Tortoise Tower, Cool Wind Pavilion, Stone Pool, and Deer Park Terrace.
idiomatic: In the fifth month he began the Purple Pole Hall, Black Tortoise Tower, Cool Wind Pavilion, Stone Pool, and Deer Park Terrace.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: ordered Pacifying the Distance General, Yanzhou Regional Inspector Zhangsun Fei with twenty thousand foot and horse south along Xuchang and Pengcheng.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he sent Zhangsun Fei with twenty thousand men south against Xuchang and Pengcheng.

literal: Ordered bestowal on garrison officers and soldiers throughout the realm of cloth and silk each according to rank.
idiomatic: He gave cloth and silk to the garrison troops according to rank.

literal: Winter, twelfth month, day xinhai: ordered Western Campaign Grand General, Prince of Changshan Zun and others to lead masses of fifty thousand to attack and defeat Duolan division chief Muyigan; Material Officers General He Tu led six thousand cavalry to raid the Chufu, Suguyan, and other tribes.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the twelfth month of winter Zun with fifty thousand men defeated Muyigan of the Duolan, while He Tu with six thousand horse raided the Chufu and Suguyan tribes.

literal: Gathered erudites and Confucian scholars, compared the masses of classic characters, meanings classified and followed one another, altogether more than forty thousand characters, titled the Collected Culture Classic.
idiomatic: He gathered scholars, standardized the script across the classics, and compiled more than forty thousand characters into the Collected Culture Classic.

literal: That year, Murong Sheng died; Bao's younger brother Xi presumptuously established himself.
idiomatic: That year Murong Sheng died and Bao's brother Xi seized the throne.

literal: Lü Guang's younger brother's son Long killed Zuan and established himself.
idiomatic: Long, nephew of Lü Guang, killed Zuan and made himself ruler.

literal: Lushui Hu Juqu Mengxun privately styled Regional Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Zhangye.
idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui Hu declared himself inspector of Liangzhou and duke of Zhangye.

literal: Mengxun and Li Gao both sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: Mengxun and Li Gao both sent envoys to court.

literal: Year 5, spring, first month, day dingchou: Murong Xi sent generals to raid Liaoxi; Tiger Might General Su Tagan and others resisted battle unfavorably, abandoned Lingzhi and returned.
idiomatic: In the fifth year, on the dingchou day of the first month of spring, Murong Xi raided Liaoxi; Su Tagan was beaten and withdrew from Lingzhi.

literal: The emperor heard Yao Xing would raid the frontier; on day gengyin, great review of carriage followers; ordered Bingzhou armies to accumulate grain at Ganbi in Pingyang.
idiomatic: Learning that Yao Xing meant to attack the frontier, on the gengyin day he reviewed the army and ordered grain stored at Ganbi in Pingyang.

literal: On day wuzi, Material Officers General He Tu defeated the Chufu, Suguyan, and other tribes, obtained more than three thousand horses, more than seventy thousand cattle and sheep.
idiomatic: On the wuzi day He Tu defeated the Chufu and Suguyan and took three thousand horses and seventy thousand head of livestock.

literal: On day xinmao, Rouran Shelun sent cavalry to rescue Suguyan and others; He Tu met and attacked them at the southern mountain river bend, obtained armored horses more than two thousand.
idiomatic: On the xinmao day Shelun of the Rouran sent horse to rescue Suguyan; He Tu met and broke them at the river bend south of the mountains and took two thousand armored horses.

literal: Withdrew the army.
idiomatic: The army withdrew.

literal: Rewards for officers and soldiers each according to merit.
idiomatic: The officers and men were rewarded.

literal: Second month, day guichou: Western Campaign Grand General, Prince of Changshan Zun and others reached Gaoping in Anding; Muyigan led several thousand horse with Weichen and Qu Fu abandoned the state and fled; pursued to Wating in Longxi, could not catch up and returned.
idiomatic: On the guichou day of the second month Zun reached Gaoping in Anding. Muyigan fled west with several thousand horse, Weichen, and Qu Fu; pursuit reached Wating in Longxi but failed to overtake them.

literal: Obtained their baggage, treasuries, more than forty thousand horses, camels and yak more than three thousand head, cattle and sheep more than ninety thousand.
idiomatic: They seized baggage and stores, forty thousand horses, three thousand camels and yaks, and ninety thousand cattle and sheep.

literal: Distributed rewards to officers and soldiers each according to merit.
idiomatic: The troops were rewarded by merit.

literal: Relocated their people to the capital.
idiomatic: Their people were moved to the capital.

literal: Monk Zhang Qiao styled himself Unsurpassed King, with Dingling Xianyu Cibao gathered parties at Xingtang in Changshan.
idiomatic: The monk Zhang Qiao styled himself Unsurpassed King and with Cibao of the Dingling raised a host at Xingtang in Changshan.

literal: Summer, fourth month: Administrator Lou Fulian attacked and beheaded him.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Administrator Lou Fulian attacked and killed him.

literal: Fifth month: Yao Xing sent his younger brother Pacifying the North General, Duke of Yiyang Ping leading masses of forty thousand to invade; Pingyang Ganbi was taken by Ping.
idiomatic: In the fifth month Yao Xing sent his brother Ping with forty thousand men; Ping took Ganbi at Pingyang.

literal: Sixth month: drilled troops at the eastern suburb, assigned the host of armies; ordered Pacifying the West Grand General Prince of Piling Shun, Zhangsun Fei, and three other generals with sixty thousand cavalry as vanguard.
idiomatic: In the sixth month he reviewed the army at the eastern suburb and named Prince Shun of Piling, Zhangsun Fei, and two other generals to lead sixty thousand horse as vanguard.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, day wuchen on the new moon: the imperial carriage western campaign.
idiomatic: On the new moon of the seventh month of autumn, the wuchen day, the court marched west.

literal: Eighth month, day yisi: reached Chaibi; Ping firmly defended; advanced army and besieged it; Yao Xing raised his entire host to rescue.
idiomatic: On the yisi day of the eighth month he reached Chaibi, invested Ping's stronghold, and Yao Xing came with his whole army.

literal: On day jiazi, the emperor crossed Meng Ravine, met and attacked Xing's army, greatly defeated them.
idiomatic: On the jiazi day he crossed Meng Ravine, met Xing's army, and won a crushing victory.

literal: Winter, tenth month: Ping went to the water and died; captured the remaining masses more than thirty thousand.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Ping drowned; more than thirty thousand of his men were taken.

literal: The account is in the biography of Xing.
idiomatic: The fuller story is told in the biography of Yao Xing.

literal: Captured Xing's Pacifying the Barbarians General, Secretariat Right Vice Director Di Bozhi, Rapid-as-Horses Commandant Tang Xiaofang, Strong Crossbow General Yao Liangguo, Establishing Loyalty General Lei Xing, Kang Guan, [12] Northern Gentlemen General Kang Wei, Ping's younger brother's son Bohun and below, fourth-rank generals and above more than forty persons.
idiomatic: He took Di Bozhi, Tang Xiaofang, Yao Liangguo, Lei Xing, Kang Guan, [12] Kang Wei, Bohun nephew of Ping, and more than forty officers of fourth rank and above.

literal: Captured former lost ministers Wang Ciduo, Jin Qin, all beheaded and displayed.
idiomatic: He also seized the defectors Wang Ciduo and Jin Qin and had them executed.

literal: Xing repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace; the emperor did not permit.
idiomatic: Xing sued repeatedly for peace; the emperor refused.

literal: The host of ministers urged advancing to pacify Puban; the emperor feared the Rouran would make trouble; on day wushen, withdrew the army.
idiomatic: His ministers urged him on to Puban, but fearing the Rouran he withdrew on the wushen day.

literal: Eleventh month: the imperial carriage halted at Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court halted at Jinyang.

literal: Summoned Yanzhou Regional Inspector Yu Yue as Minister of Works.
idiomatic: Yu Yue, inspector of Yanzhou, was summoned to be minister of works.

literal: Sent Left General Mo Ti to attack Shangdang bandits Qin Po, Dingling Zhai Du at Huguan.
idiomatic: Mo Ti was sent against the bandits Qin Po and Zhai Du of the Dingling at Huguan.

literal: On day dingchou, Shangdang Administrator captured Po and beheaded him; Du fled to Linyu.
idiomatic: On the dingchou day the administrator of Shangdang captured and killed Po; Du fled to Linyu.

literal: Twelfth month, day xinhai: returned from the western campaign.
idiomatic: On the xinhai day of the twelfth month he returned from the western campaign.

literal: Rouran Shelun violated the frontier; ordered Prince of Changshan Zun to pursue, could not catch up and returned.
idiomatic: Shelun of the Rouran raided the frontier; Zun pursued but could not overtake him.

literal: Yueqin Mofu led his division of more than ten thousand households to submit within the borders, dwelling north of Wuyuan.
idiomatic: Yueqin Mofu submitted with more than ten thousand households and was settled north of Wuyuan.

literal: That year, Tufa Lugu died of illness; younger brother Rutan took overall charge, sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: That year Tufa Lugu died; his brother Rutan succeeded him and sent envoys to court.

literal: Year 6, spring, first month, day xinwei: Shuofang Yuchi division separate commander led more than ten thousand households to submit within the borders, entering to dwell in Yunzhong.
idiomatic: In the sixth year, on the xinwei day of the first month of spring, a Yuchi sub-chief of Shuofang submitted with more than ten thousand households and was settled in Yunzhong.

literal: Summer, fifth month: great review of carriage followers, intending to strike the Jiang and Huai, pacify the disorder of Jing and Yang.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he reviewed the army, intending to march on the Jiang and Huai and pacify the south.

literal: Autumn, seventh month: Pacifying the West Grand General, Director of the Secretariat, Prince of Piling Shun had crime, demoted to prince and returned to his estate.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Prince Shun of Piling was found guilty, stripped of office, and sent to his estate.

literal: On day wuzi, the imperial carriage northern tour, built a detached palace at Chai Mountain, released soldiers to hunt in competition, northeast crossed Gui Ridge, exited Canhe and Dai valleys.
idiomatic: On the wuzi day he toured north, built a lodge on Chai Mountain, held a great hunt, crossed Gui Ridge northeast, and passed through Canhe and Dai.

literal: Ninth month: traveled to Nanping City, planned the south of Lei, faced Xiawu Mountain, backed on Huangguadui, intending to build a new city.
idiomatic: In the ninth month he went to Nanping, surveyed the country south of Lei below Xiawu Mountain and Huangguadui, and planned a new capital.

literal: On day xinwei, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
idiomatic: On the xinwei day he returned to the palace.

literal: Winter, tenth month: began the Western Zhaoyang Hall.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he began the Western Zhaoyang Hall.

literal: On day yimao, established the imperial son Si as Prince of Qi, added General of Chariots and Cavalry, rank equal to the prime minister.
idiomatic: On the yimao day he made the prince Si prince of Qi, general of chariots and cavalry, and equal in rank to the prime minister.

literal: Shao as Prince of Qinghe, added Grand General Southern Campaign.
idiomatic: Shao was made prince of Qinghe and grand general southern campaign.

literal: Xi as Prince of Yangping.
idiomatic: Xi was made prince of Yangping.

literal: Yao as Prince of Henan.
idiomatic: Yao was made prince of Henan.

literal: Enfeoffed former Prince of Qin Min's son Kui as Prince of Yuzhang, Chenliu Prince's son Right General Yue as Prince of Zhuti.
idiomatic: Kui, son of the former Prince Min of Qin, was made prince of Yuzhang; Yue, son of the prince of Chenliu, was made prince of Zhuti.

literal: On day dingsi, ordered General Yi Wei to lead twenty thousand cavalry north to raid the Gaoche.
idiomatic: On the dingsi day Yi Wei was ordered north with twenty thousand horse against the Gaoche.

literal: Sima Dezong sent envoys with court tribute.
idiomatic: Sima Dezong sent envoys to court.

literal: Eleventh month, day gengwu: Yi Wei greatly defeated the Gaoche.
idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the eleventh month Yi Wei routed the Gaoche.

literal: That year, the island barbarian Huan Xuan deposed his lord Sima Dezong and established himself, presumptuously styled Great Chu.
idiomatic: That year Huan Xuan of the eastern isles deposed Sima Dezong and declared himself emperor of Great Chu.

literal: Tianci year 1, spring, first month: sent Lishi Protecting Army Liu Tuo leading three thousand cavalry to raid Puzi.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tianci, in the first month of spring, Liu Tuo was sent with three thousand horse to raid Puzi.

literal: Third month, day bingyin: captured Yao Xing's Pacifying the North General, Taiping Administrator Heng Tan, obtained more than three thousand persons.
idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the third month he took Heng Tan, Xing's pacifying-the-north general and administrator of Taiping, with more than three thousand men.
